topic.title: Next recharge hike will not be called a hike
topic.claim: The next recharge hike will likely come dressed as 'usage-based plans', so heavy users feel it first and nobody calls it a rise.
topic.behaviour: We top up an 84-day plan, forget the price, and notice only when it gets a new name.
topic.mechanism: A change that splits users into light and heavy lets the company say most people are unaffected. The people who pay more are the ones who are using data, which is most of us.
topic.group: Prepaid users on Jio, Airtel and Vi plans
topic.moment: You recharge for 84 days and do not remember what you paid last time.

turn.believed: Telecom prices go up in one big announced jump.
turn.actually: They can shift quietly through plan design, so each user feels a different rise.

topic.feeling: Squeezed, with no easy way to compare
topic.villain: A tariff structure that hides price rises inside plan design
topic.because: Operators earn more per user when heavy data users pay more. A split-up plan makes complaining harder because nobody has the same bill.

proof.fact: Cashify reports that Jio, Airtel and Vi may raise prepaid prices by up to 15% within the next 3 to 4 months. This is an expectation, not a confirmed hike, and pricing may move towards usage-based charging. Current 84-day plans cost Rs 519 for Jio and Vi and Rs 539 for Airtel.

topic.payoff: Screenshot your plan price today. In a few months you will know whether the rise was a rise.
topic.send_to: The friend who streams all day on mobile data and never looks at the plan
real_details: The page says the last major tariff change was about two years ago, in 2024.
topic.news_peg: On 17 November 2026 Cashify reported that prepaid plans may cost up to 15% more in the next 3 to 4 months, which is an expectation and not a confirmed hike.
topic.why_now: The expected hike is the next thing to land on a bill most of us pay without looking.

slides.why_swipe: Who exactly is the heavy user?

paragraphs:
So who counts as heavy? Look at your own week:
– the hotspot for your laptop every time the flat's Wi-Fi dies
– reels on every cab ride
– the Sunday video call with your parents
Heavy user is just another name for a normal one.
slides.why_swipe: Is paying for what you use actually unfair?

paragraphs: To be fair, paying for what you use sounds right. Someone on a basic phone shouldn't fund your streaming.
But rename the plan and the old price disappears. Nothing is left to compare the new one to.
slides.why_swipe: So how do you catch it?

paragraphs: Screenshot your plan price today. ₹519, ₹539, whatever yours says.
When the new plan lands, run your same week through it: the hotspot, the cab reels, the Sunday call. That screenshot is the only proof it went up.

draft.alt_text: A ten-slide text post arguing that the next mobile recharge hike in India will arrive as usage-based plans rather than a single announced jump. It notes current 84-day prepaid plans cost ₹519 on Jio and Vi and ₹539 on Airtel, and that Cashify expects prices could rise by up to 15% in 3 to 4 months, possibly priced by usage, with no date announced. Unlike the July 2024 hike, which was a headline everyone felt together, a split plan lets the company make more from heavy users, point to light users who pay nothing extra, and avoid one shared complaint. It argues that heavy use, like hotspots, reels in cabs and Sunday video calls, is normal use, and that a renamed plan removes the old price to compare against. It ends by asking readers to screenshot their current plan price, since that screenshot will be the only proof the price went up.

claims.text: An 84-day prepaid plan costs ₹519 on Jio and Vi, and ₹539 on Airtel.
Cashify says Jio, Airtel and Vi could raise prepaid prices by up to 15% in the next 3 to 4 months; no date is announced yet.
The report says pricing may move towards usage-based charging, where users who consume more data pay more.
The last headline tariff hike was in July 2024 and was openly announced as a rise across headline rates.
